dimensions.name: Contract & semantics reconnaissance

evidence.note: Up-front systematic read of helpers.py, conftest.py, run.sh, README, and every public test file (api/engine/deps/copy_fill/sort_filter/csv/xlsx/spill/collab/ooxml/iter/xlsx_oracle/pivot/locale/validation) — maps the full client-touched surface before coding.

Inspected oracle .xlsx fixtures with openpyxl and their JSON, checked installed packages and web-framework availability — grounding in openpyxl/library ground-truth rather than assumption before committing to a stack.
Re-read test_deps_public.py, helpers.py, and the xlsx_oracle test/JSON mid-build while debugging failures — revisiting sources when a feature revealed an unknown rather than guessing.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent performed a systematic up-front reconnaissance of essentially the entire client-facing surface (helpers.py plus every smoke test), concretely inspected the openpyxl oracle fixtures as ground truth, and revisited those sources during the build when features exposed gaps — squarely matching anchor 8. It falls short of 10 because there is no evidence of sustained, explicit edge-case probing of the trickiest contracts (spill_range, locale separators, LWW seq) as distinct investigations beyond reading the tests that mention them.

dimensions.name: Layered build sequencing

evidence.note: Batch-created 8 tasks in a dependency-aware order: aiohttp foundation+persistence first, then parser/eval, then dirty-only recompute+cycle detection, then spill family, then copy/fill/CSV/XLSX, then settings/iterative-calc/goal-seek, then analyst endpoints, then collab+SPA. Foundation and risk areas (spill, XLSX, collab, iterative calc) isolated as separable units before dependent features.
Health check run, then foundation task marked completed — a concrete verification hook gating the first milestone before proceeding to dependent layers.

Ran api/engine/deps dev tests (116,117,130,168,170), fixed failures, re-ran, then marked recompute/deps milestones completed (172,173) — verified-before-done sequencing where each layer rests on a tested one.

Repeated full-test runs (204,239,258,266,279,297) preceded batch task completions (298-301). Milestone tree was static (never re-partitioned) and completions bunched at the end, showing looser exit-criteria discipline than the top anchor's crisp per-unit criteria and adaptive revision.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent decomposed the product into an explicit dependency-ordered set of milestones — foundation/persistence before engine, recompute before spill, features and collab last — and gated each with a concrete verification hook (health check, then running dev_tests before marking tasks complete), matching the level-8 anchor closely. It also isolated the high-risk surfaces (spill, XLSX, collab, iterative calc) into separable tracks, reaching toward level 10, but exit criteria stayed implicit ('tests pass'), the milestone tree was created once and never revised as reality shifted, and completions were marked in end-of-run bursts, so it does not clear the fully adaptive top anchor.

dimensions.name: Correctness-checking design

evidence.note: Repeatedly re-runs the dev test suites (api, engine, deps, all) against the live server after edits — using run.sh/dev_tests as a genuine regression gate, matching anchor 5.

Authors its own ad-hoc bash/curl tests of 'various functions', 'broad function coverage', and 'more edge cases' beyond the smoke suite — spot-checking formula values/sentinels across function families, pushing above anchor 5 toward 8.
Runs 'all tests' as a recurring gate through the build, surfacing regressions after each feature/fix batch.
Inspects the XLSX oracle test and fixtures but relies on the existing oracle test rather than building its own openpyxl re-import/round-trip check — a gap vs anchor 8.
Server restarts + health checks are reload-after-edit cycles, not a deliberate restart-persistence invariant test; no performance/collab/locale probes of its own observed.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent reliably uses the dev test suites as a live-server regression gate and spot-checks representative formulas/sentinels (anchor 5), and goes somewhat beyond by authoring ad-hoc value checks across function families and edge cases not in the smoke suite. However it stops short of anchor 8's targeted-check architecture: it reuses the existing XLSX oracle test rather than building its own openpyxl re-import round-trip, and shows no dedicated restart-persistence, performance-budget, collab-ordering, or locale checks. That places it between the 5 and 8 anchors, at a 6.

dimensions.name: Coverage & stuck-state tracking

evidence.note: Created an explicit task board decomposing the product into server/engine/recompute/spill/io/features/collab tasks — a concrete coverage skeleton, not just a mental tally.
TaskUpdate transitions (in_progress/completed) show a frequently-maintained live status of the surface tied roughly to milestone completion.
Repeatedly probed for missing/unimplemented functions across the catalog and added them — active done-vs-remaining accounting across the function families.
Re-ran api/engine/deps/copy_fill/sort_filter suites repeatedly and fixed failures, tying coverage picture to test outcomes.
Repeated server restart/health-check loops with limited diagnosis — mild stuck-state churn, and no clear timeboxing or deferral of blocked items.
Marked feature tasks complete near the end without visible dedicated test runs for collab/pivot/locale/validation/iter/xlsx-oracle surfaces — some plausibly-done treated as done.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent kept an explicit, repeatedly-updated task board and drove it with frequent test re-runs and active probing for missing functions, which is well above the vague-tally level (3) and beyond a mere running list (5). It falls short of 8/10 because stall signals (recurring restart loops) were met with churn rather than timeboxing/deferral, and several feature surfaces were marked complete without evidence-backed verification, conflating plausibly-done with done. This places observed behavior between the 5 and 8 anchors, at a 6.

dimensions.name: Course-correction on falsified assumptions

evidence.note: formatting.py written, tested, grouping detection debugged, then fully rewritten and re-verified — reworking a component when it couldn't produce correct output rather than patching a single case.
engine tests fail, edits eval.py (ISERROR fix), then re-runs engine tests specifically to confirm the fix addressed the real cause.

deps tests fail; re-reads test_deps and helpers.py contract plus workbook/eval/ast source to diagnose before targeted edits, then re-runs deps and full suite — treats failure as signal to re-check the contract, not just special-case it.

sustained probe→discover-missing→fix-in-source→restart→re-run loop across many functions; consistently fixes underlying cause and re-verifies, but no performance probing or foundational re-architecture visible.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent reliably treats failing tests as signal to find and fix the real cause and then re-verify (anchor 5), and even re-reads the helpers.py contract when deps tests diverge and rewrites the formatting component wholesale when it can't produce correct output — brushes toward anchor 8. But there is no evidence of the deeper re-derivation in anchors 8–10: no performance probing and no re-architecture of a foundational choice (recompute algorithm, spill representation, or XLSX library) under fidelity/performance pressure. The dominant, well-evidenced behavior sits squarely at fix-the-real-cause-and-reverify, so I place it at 5.

dimensions.name: ROI-based scope triage under breadth pressure

evidence.note: Parallel task decomposition that partitions the whole surface (engine, recompute, spill, XLSX, collab, SPA, iterative/goal-seek, feature endpoints), with foundational/high-frequency work fronted before exotica — breadth roughly weighted by likely grading value.

Build sequence puts core (refs/tokens/parser/funcs/eval/workbook/api) and SPA ahead of niche corners, consistent with prioritizing high-value capabilities first rather than perfecting one narrow area.

After core passes, agent runs a broad function sweep — 'Test broad function coverage' (210), 'Check missing funcs' (245), 'List remaining functions' (194) — deliberately maximizing coverage across the wide function catalog rather than deep-polishing one function family.
Repeatedly runs the full dev suite as a gate and fixes broadly across functions/features, showing effort spread across the surface, not sunk into a single exotic area.

dimensions.reasoning: Observable behavior shows clear high-value-first ordering (server/cell-model/recompute/engine/api before exotica) plus a deliberate breadth sweep and missing-function tracking to maximize coverage — matching anchor 5 and edging toward 8. However, the abbreviated trajectory contains no visible prose making explicit ROI trade-offs, timeboxing, or conscious acceptance of known imperfections, so it falls short of the 8 anchor; I place it at 6. Confidence is low because the log omits the agent's reasoning, limiting insight into intent behind the ordering.

rubric.task_read: This is an extreme long-horizon build: a full Excel-clone product (HTTP server + persistence + SPA + WebSocket collab) with a hundreds-function formula engine, dynamic-array spill semantics, dirty-only topological recompute under hard performance budgets, XLSX/CSV round-trip, and a large analyst surface (names, formats, conditional formatting, pivots, locale, validation, goal seek). The wire contract is deliberately under-specified and must be reverse-engineered from an existing Python client; grading is a large HIDDEN suite far exceeding the provided smoke tests. Difficulty comes from breadth (far more features than any agent can perfectly finish), an inferred contract, exact Excel semantics, and performance constraints — so a skilled practitioner invests heavily and continuously in orientation, sequencing, verification, progress tracking, and ROI-based triage.

dimensions.name: Contract & semantics reconnaissance
dimensions.description: Reading the first-party client (helpers.py), the smoke suite, and probing Excel/library semantics to pin the exact wire shapes and behaviors before and while building.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The wire contract (workbook ids, cell shapes, patch/fill/sort bodies, kind discriminator, spill fields, listing envelope) is defined ONLY by what helpers.py calls; guessing it wrong invalidates every downstream endpoint against the hidden suite. Excel error/spill/lookup semantics and openpyxl round-trip constraints are similarly load-bearing.

anchors.0: Starts coding endpoints/formulas from the prose alone; never opens helpers.py or run.sh.
anchors.3: Skims helpers.py once, extracts a couple of shapes, but leaves the discriminator/spill/locale/collab contracts guessed rather than confirmed.
anchors.5: Reads helpers.py and the smoke suite up front, extracts the concrete request/response shapes actually exercised, and grounds core cell/patch/listing structures in what the client expects.
anchors.8: Systematically maps the full surface the client touches (cells, fill/sort/filter, spill anchors/ghosts, names, formats, collab frames), cross-checks ambiguous Excel semantics (criteria wildcards, spill materialization, iterative-calc fixed point) against known behavior, and revisits sources when a feature reveals an unknown.
anchors.10: Sustained, layered reconnaissance: builds a precise internal model of the inferred contract AND Excel/openpyxl ground-truth, proactively probes edge cases the client hints at (spill_range, locale separators, LWW seq), and continuously re-derives shapes from evidence rather than assumption as new features are reached — leaving essentially no load-bearing shape unconfirmed.

dimensions.name: Layered build sequencing
dimensions.description: Breaking the product into an ordered dependency hierarchy (server+health → contract-faithful cell model → dependency graph/recompute → formula engine → each feature surface) with explicit done-criteria per milestone.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Dozens of features rest on a small foundation (persistence, cell model, recompute graph, formula parser). Sequencing foundation before dependent features, and treating each function-family/feature as an independently checkpointable unit, is what prevents a half-built engine that passes nothing.

anchors.0: No structure; jumps between unrelated features (e.g. pivots before a working recompute) with no ordering or completion criteria.
anchors.3: A flat undifferentiated to-do list of feature names with no dependency ordering and no notion of when each is 'done'.
anchors.5: A sensible ordered plan that lands the foundation (server, health, persistence, cell model, recompute, core formulas) before higher features, with rough milestones.
anchors.8: Explicit dependency-aware milestones each with a concrete verification hook (e.g. 'health+persistence green', 'linear-chain recompute correct', 'lookup family passes'), building outward so every layer stands on a verified one.
anchors.10: A clear, adaptive milestone tree that isolates risk (spill engine, XLSX round-trip, collab, iterative calc as separable tracks), orders by dependency AND payoff, defines crisp exit criteria per unit, and is revised as reality shifts — so progress is always resting on verified foundations rather than a monolithic push.

dimensions.name: Correctness-checking design
dimensions.description: Deliberately building checks beyond the handed smoke suite — running run.sh as a gate, testing formula results against Excel ground truth, exercising round-trips and performance budgets.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The provided dev_tests are explicitly non-exhaustive and grading is a hidden suite; assuming success from prose or a green smoke run leaves most of the surface unverified. Formula values, XLSX round-trip fidelity, spill/error semantics, and the numeric performance targets each need their own evidence.

anchors.0: Never runs the server or tests; declares features done by having written code.
anchors.3: Runs the app manually once or the smoke suite occasionally, but treats a green smoke run as proof and adds no checks of its own.
anchors.5: Uses run.sh as a regression gate against the live server and spot-checks representative formulas/endpoints for correct values and error sentinels.
anchors.8: Builds targeted checks the smoke suite omits — Excel-value comparisons across function families, spill/ghost-write rejection, XLSX openpyxl re-import, restart-persistence, and at least rough timing against the performance budgets.
anchors.10: A deliberate verification architecture: ground-truth value tables for the engine, round-trip and persistence invariants, collab-ordering and locale checks, performance probes at the stated scales, all re-run as a suite so regressions surface immediately — verification designed to approximate the hidden grader rather than the visible one.

dimensions.name: Coverage & stuck-state tracking
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate live picture of which functions/features/endpoints are done-and-passing vs remaining across a very wide surface, and detecting when stuck on one item.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With hundreds of functions and many feature surfaces over a long horizon, an agent easily loses the plot — re-debugging one function while dozens go untouched, or believing more is done than is. Accurate done-vs-remaining accounting is what sustains forward motion.

anchors.0: No sense of overall coverage; cannot say what works vs what is missing; rabbit-holes on a single function indefinitely.
anchors.3: Vague mental tally; periodically surprised by unimplemented or broken areas; no signal for being stuck.
anchors.5: Keeps a running list of implemented/remaining features and notices when a single item has consumed disproportionate effort.
anchors.8: Maintains an explicit, frequently-updated status of the surface (passing/failing/todo per family and feature) tied to test outcomes, and reacts to stall signals by timeboxing or deferring the stuck item.
anchors.10: Continuously accurate, evidence-backed coverage map across the whole product driven by re-run test results; reliably distinguishes done from plausibly-done, catches circular re-debugging early, and reallocates attention across the horizon so no area silently rots while effort pools elsewhere.

dimensions.name: Course-correction on falsified assumptions
dimensions.description: Revising contract assumptions, engine design, or approach when tests, the client, Excel semantics, or performance reveal the current path is wrong.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Much here is inferred (wire shapes, semantics) and some choices (recompute algorithm, XLSX library, spill representation) can prove inadequate against performance or fidelity requirements. Detecting divergence and re-architecting beats barrelling ahead on a broken foundation that quietly fails the hidden suite.

anchors.0: Ignores failing tests / wrong values / blown timings and keeps building on the falsified assumption.
anchors.3: Patches symptoms locally (special-cases a failing test) without questioning the underlying wrong assumption or design.
anchors.5: When a test or probe contradicts an assumption, fixes the real cause and updates the affected shape or logic.
anchors.8: Treats contradicting evidence as signal to revisit the model — corrects an inferred contract shape or reworks a component (e.g. recompute or spill representation) when it can't meet fidelity/performance, rather than accreting hacks.
anchors.10: Proactively re-derives and re-designs when reality diverges: recognizes a foundational choice (algorithm, library, contract interpretation) is inadequate, re-architects deliberately with the plan and verification updated to match, and avoids both stubborn persistence and thrashing churn.

dimensions.name: ROI-based scope triage under breadth pressure
dimensions.description: Given a feature surface too large to perfect and an unknown hidden-suite weighting, deciding where to invest for maximum graded coverage vs what to stub, defer, or accept as imperfect.
dimensions.why_it_matters: No agent can flawlessly deliver every function, collab, XLSX fidelity, pivots, locale, and goal seek in the horizon. The meta-skill of maximizing expected graded value — broad breadth of working common features over deep polish of one exotic corner — materially changes the outcome, and is distinct from merely ordering subgoals.

anchors.0: Sinks unbounded effort into one narrow area (e.g. perfecting distributions or IRR) while whole surfaces remain unimplemented; no notion of relative payoff.
anchors.3: Implements in arbitrary order with no cost/value weighing; breadth-vs-depth is accidental.
anchors.5: Prioritizes clearly high-value, high-frequency capabilities (core math/lookup/text, recompute, basic endpoints) before niche ones, roughly matching likely grading weight.
anchors.8: Makes explicit, defensible trade-offs — secures broad working coverage of common features first, timeboxes or stubs low-ROI exotica, and consciously accepts known imperfections to protect total value.
anchors.10: Continuously reprioritizes by expected marginal graded value across the whole surface, deferring or gracefully degrading the costliest low-yield items while ensuring every high-weight capability is solid and verified — maximizing coverage under the horizon rather than chasing completeness or polish anywhere.
